{{Recipe summary
| Category = Soup recipes
| Difficulty = 3
}}

{{recipe}}

==Ingredients==
* Green [[Cookbook:Split Pea|split peas]]
* Streaky pork belly [[Cookbook:Bacon|bacon]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] small
* [[Cookbook:Pork|Pork]] belly slices (non smoked), [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]] into small strips
* Dutch smoked [[Cookbook:Sausage|sausage]] (if not available any smoked sausage will do), sliced small
* 1 large [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrot]], [[Cookbook:Cube|cubed]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Leek|leek]], sliced into rings
* 1 [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], chopped
* ½ [[Cookbook:Celery Root|celeriac]], cubed
* 3 [[Cookbook:Potato|potatoes]], cubed
* 2 [[Cookbook:Bay Leaf|bay leaves]]

==Procedure==

#Soak the split peas in water overnight.
#[[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] the pork belly slices in a [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]] until golden brown (but not too crispy).
#Cook the peas in enough water for about 30 minutes. Make sure to remove foam from the pan with a spoon.
#In another pan, cook the bacon and the fried pork belly slices together with the vegetables, some salt and pepper, and the bay leaves for about 45 minutes.
#When the erwtensoep is ready, add the Dutch smoked sausage, and [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] it for another 15 minutes.
#As a finishing touch, add some fried dried onions.

steps.text: Soak the split peas in water overnight.
Fry the pork belly slices in a frying pan until golden brown (but not too crispy).
Cook the peas in enough water for about 30 minutes. Make sure to remove foam from the pan with a spoon.
In another pan, cook the bacon and the fried pork belly slices together with the vegetables, some salt and pepper, and the bay leaves for about 45 minutes.
When the erwtensoep is ready, add the Dutch smoked sausage, and boil it for another 15 minutes.
As a finishing touch, add some fried dried onions.
